description: Reads from and writes to Apache Kafka topics.

options.label: Topic
options.help: Topic to read from or write to.

options.label: Bootstrap servers
options.help: Comma-separated broker list.

options.label: Consumer group
options.help: Required for sources. Pick a name unique to this job, or it will share offsets with another.

options.label: Start reading from
options.help: Where a source begins when it has no committed offset.

options.label: Format
options.help: How records are encoded. avro-confluent is the usual choice on Kafka: the schema lives in a registry and each message carries its id. Plain avro is for topics written without one, and then the columns below are the schema. Avro needs its jars in the image -- see scripts/fetch-formats.sh.

options.label: Schema registry URL
options.help: Where the registry is, as reachable from the TaskManager. Leave blank to use the registry configured under Schema registry.

options.label: Subject
options.help: Which subject a sink registers its schema under. Sources do not need it: each message names its own schema by id.

options.label: Registry credentials
options.help: user:password, when the registry needs it. Store it as a secret.

options.label: Ignore parse errors
options.help: Skip malformed records instead of failing the job. Off by default: silent data loss is rarely what you want.

options.label: Partitioner
options.help: How produced records are assigned to partitions.

options.label: Delivery guarantee
options.help: How hard this sink works to not lose or duplicate records. At-least-once flushes on every checkpoint and may write a record twice after a failure. Exactly-once wraps each checkpoint in a Kafka transaction, so readers set to read_committed see each record once, at the cost of latency: nothing is visible until the checkpoint completes. None is fire and forget.

options.label: Transactional id prefix
options.help: Required for exactly-once, and must be unique per job. Two jobs sharing a prefix will fence each other's transactions off and neither will make progress.

options.label: Acknowledgements
options.help: How many brokers must confirm a write before Kafka calls it done. 'all' waits for every in-sync replica and is the only setting that survives a broker failure. '1' waits for the leader alone. '0' does not wait, which means Flink cannot tell whether a record arrived -- that silently defeats any delivery guarantee above.

options.label: Compression
options.help: Compresses batches before they are sent. zstd and lz4 usually pay for themselves on JSON, which compresses well.

options.label: Transaction timeout (ms)
options.help: Must be longer than the checkpoint interval, or a transaction expires before its checkpoint completes and the job loses data. It must also not exceed the broker's transaction.max.timeout.ms, which defaults to 15 minutes -- the broker rejects anything larger.

options.label: Linger (ms)
options.help: How long the producer waits to fill a batch before sending. Raising it trades latency for throughput.

options.label: Batch size (bytes)
options.help: Maximum bytes per batch per partition.

options.label: Max records per poll
options.help: How many records a source fetches at a time. Only worth changing when a source is the bottleneck.

options.label: Isolation level
options.help: Set read_committed when reading a topic written by an exactly-once producer; otherwise this source will see records from transactions that were later aborted.

options.label: SASL JAAS config
options.help: Full JAAS line. Store it as a secret and reference it here.
